headline: Learned models transfer and align transcriptomic profiles across samples and modalities
label: Transcriptomics Representation Learning
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply domain adaptation, contrastive learning and foundation-model embeddings to recover or interpret transcriptomic profiles.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned models that transfer information across samples, modalities or spatial neighborhoods to recover or interpret transcriptomic profiles. FFPERescuer applies unsupervised domain adaptation to reconstruct expression from degraded FFPE tumor samples, and FOCST predicts spatial transcriptomics from histology using UNI embeddings, a graph neural network and contrastive learning. spAlignDE performs cross-sample and cross-modal spatial alignment with mismatch-aware differential expression, while SpaCoEx selects sparse genes with spatially varying co-expression. scFLAME unifies embedding, clustering and marker-gene identification in one negative-binomial factor model, and scOLAR performs ontology-anchored open-set annotation. An independent benchmark reports poor H&E-based single-cell expression prediction in skin. The items do not share a common evaluation; what appears new is explicit handling of domain shift, mismatch and benchmarking within transcriptomic inference.
